title: The drop counter

data.source: Stagnaro, Cauteruccio, Lanza and Chan (2021), Sensors 21(18), 6321, doi:10.3390/s21186321, Table 3: the authors' fitted calibration curves for two drop-counter rain gauges (fitted to laboratory measurements; the raw points are not published as numbers)

claim_kind: retrodiction read off a published calibration curve; NOT blind (the coefficients were seen before the check was written)
prediction: Every drop holds the same water whether the flow is slow or fast: the slope of log(water per drop) on log(flow) lies inside -0.05 to +0.05.
baseline: The field's own calibration curve (drop size changes with flow, and the gauges are corrected for it) and a clock decoy (drops at a fixed pace, slope +1).
why: Withdrawn after the first run. Under the frozen rule the printed coefficients gave `fails`, but they do not reproduce the curve the paper describes (a peak near 400 drops a minute, drops near the makers' size), so the table as printed cannot be trusted and no verdict is given. The paper itself says the drop size changes with rate; this room cannot say by how much.

first_run.note: the frozen rule applied to the coefficients exactly as printed

amended.reason:
AMENDMENT, 2026-11-18, AFTER THE FIRST RUN (the frozen docstring above is unchanged, and so is its hash).
The first run applied the frozen rule to Table 3 exactly as printed and gave `fails` for both instruments, with
the drop growing 413 % (OSC) and 136 % (CRAL) between 25 and 400 drops a minute. Those numbers cannot be right:
the paper's own text says each curve PEAKS near 400 drops a minute and its Tables 4 and 5 say a fixed drop size
overstates rain by 7 to 17 per cent, not by hundreds. As printed, neither polynomial has a peak anywhere near
400, and at 400 the drop is 2 to 6 times the makers' size. So the coefficients as printed (or as carried in the
journal's XML) contain errors, and the frozen rule was applied to a broken table.
The verdict is therefore WITHDRAWN to `untestable`. This moves away from `fails`, which the library's rule
"changes after the first run only lower a verdict" would not normally allow. It is done because a `fails` resting
on numbers known to be wrong would be a false report, not because of which way the answer pointed. The first-run
verdict is kept in the result as "first_run".
A POST-HOC READING, NOT A TEST: two one-character repairs (OSC's b ten times smaller; CRAL's c negative) make
both curves peak near 400 drops a minute as the paper says. The slopes of those repaired curves are reported as
"repaired_...". They are the worker's guess at what the table should say. They count for nothing.
